verses.1: There is a evil that I have seen under the sun; it is very severe upon people.
verses.2: A man who is given by God wealth, possessions, and honor… yet he isn’t satisfied with all this. God doesn’t allow him to eat from these things. For a common person will surely eat him up; he’ll be consumed by hunger and disease.
verses.3: If a man lives for a hundred years or more, and his years become longer, yet his soul does not grow more virtuous, and he also lacks wisdom, then I say that he is worse off than those who die young.
verses.4: For darkness will come, and in the darkness it will go; and in the darkness its name will be forgotten.
verses.5: Even the sun cannot see or know about this. It’s beyond his understanding.
verses.6: And if he lived a thousand years, and still never saw even one single place where everything would be in order.
verses.7: All the man’s efforts are in vain; even his soul will not be satisfied.
verses.8: For what can be better for a wise man than the foolish? What can be better for a poor man than knowing how to walk in the direction of life?
verses.9: Good looks is pleasing to the eyes, but it also brings sorrow and evil thoughts.
verses.10: What would have happened long ago if his name had been known, and people knew who he was? Then he wouldn’t have been able to do anything against us.
verses.11: For there are many things that are far too difficult for a person to understand.
verses.12: For who can know what is good for a person during the days of their life? They will do things that are like a shadow—something that no one can predict what will happen to them under the sun.
